title: Learn a document you weren't given: streaming SME simulation on Amazon review moderation
description:
## Purpose

"Learn a document you weren't given." Demonstrate the owner's target use case: a self-learning classifier with NO starting dataset, only a one-line description. Decisions arrive in a stream (batches as small as 1). A simulated SME reviews SOME fraction of decisions and gives the correct label plus a one-sentence explanation. The flywheel uses every lever: the fixed few-shot example list, the questions Jev is asked (feature discovery), and refitting the ML head over Jev's answers.

Source of truth: approved plan `~/.claude/plans/i-put-you-in-sprightly-penguin.md` (owner-approved 2026-10-02).

## Why this experiment

Across 5 real human-labeled datasets Jev either already knew the rubric (HateCheck one-liner 0.97, CAP) or could not apply it even when handed it (FOMC 0.656 -> 0.684, EDOS, SwDA). On FOMC the mechanism moved the needle (simulated explanations recovered ~92% of a tiny gap vs ~40-47% labels-only/shuffled; all gains in round 1). We need a domain with a large, learnable gap; we control that by having an LLM SME apply a detailed written policy to real texts.

## Owner decisions

- Classifier starts with a ONE-LINE description S: "Moderate an Amazon product review: approve, or flag as abusive, promotional, seller_shipping, or price_availability."
- The SME LLM holds the FULL written policy F (~900 words, precedence abusive > promotional > seller_shipping > price_availability > approve, rules R1..R12); the classifier never sees it.
- Domain: Amazon review moderation on real Amazon reviews (McAuley Lab "Amazon Reviews 2023"; Cell_Phones_and_Accessories, Home_and_Kitchen, Toys_and_Games; 2013-2016; 15-90 words).
- NO drift in experiment 1 (drift = experiment 2, separate note task).

## Arms

- **B**: S only, no learning (floor; free alongside E).
- **L**: labels only, all levers (plain disagreements count toward the steering trigger).
- **E**: labels + SME explanations, all levers.
- **X**: explanations shuffled among reviewed items (shows content matters).
- Optional **E at p = 1.0** if spend allows.

Review rate p = 0.3 (uniform, propensity recorded); stream 600 items, held-out 300; floor Jev+S, ceiling Jev+F. Prequential accuracy and macro-F1 (windowed 100 and cumulative) vs reviewed items; held-out scored through frozen bundles after 300 stream items and at the end; bootstrap CIs via `unified_stats`.

## Budget

**Hard total ~$10** (Jev + OpenAI). Rough: ~7,500 Jev requests (~$4-7) + OpenAI ~$2-3. Per-stage ledgers with hard ceilings; Jev spend authorized within caps.

## Stop points

- After L0: owner confirms dataset license/terms before any download.
- After Stage 0 (screen gate): **STOP, owner looks.**
- After Stage 1 (arm E + B): **STOP, owner looks.**
- Stage 2 (L, X, optional E at p=1.0) then publish.

## What result changes what we build

- Screen fails -> change the label set or the domain.
- E ~ L -> explanations add nothing at this rate; try active sampling / higher review rate next.
- E >> L and X -> the stakeholder channel teaches the unwritten document; proceed to drift (experiment 2).
- Gains only at the first refit (as on FOMC) -> loosen the promotion gate / steering thresholds before experiment 2.

## Honest caveats (must appear in results)

- Gold labels come from an LLM SME: this measures "learning this SME's policy", not human truth.
- The stream's class mix is enriched (natural mix also reported).
- One stream order: cannot resolve differences below ~5 F1 points.
- Real SMEs are vaguer and less consistent than an LLM.

## Working rules (owner)

- Opus sub-agents build offline in small steps (specs first, fakes, no network in specs; planted/Emotion/FOMC replays stay byte-identical; Jev-Flywheel checkout untouched). Main session reviews (tests, byte-identical replays on copies, push, confirm remote) and runs live stages.
- Questions to the owner plainly at the top; results as one small table.
- Record provenance, not text: review and policy text stay under gitignored `var/`/`.data/`; commit only IDs, hashes and text-free summaries.

## Unverified (owner to confirm)

- Amazon Reviews 2023 license/terms; redistribution of Amazon guideline pages.
- gpt-6-sol availability/pricing (else gpt-6-luna, noted).
- Whether `abusive` is frequent enough to keep as its own class (merge into "remove_other" if < 20 pool cases).

## Definition of done

Stage 2 published: one results page with prequential curves, checkpoint table, spend table and caveats; decision recorded on the next build (per "What result changes what we build"); tasks closed with evidence.
